## Cubed-sphere face-state seam sync {#sec-ch03-cslrsync}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: before the $x_2$ and $x_3$ Riemann solves, the reconstructed left and right states at panel-edge faces are
exchanged as raw copies, one face deep, so that both panels solve the same Riemann problem at a shared face.
**Switch**: none. **Default**: always on with `layout: cubed-sphere`. **Requires**: the direction-suffixed keys
`*_wl:+` and `*_wr:-`. **Order**: exact copy. **Defining rule**: the suffix rule of the Derivation layer.
:::

At a face between two panels, each panel reconstructs the state on its own side from its interior and the state on
the other side from its interpolated ghosts. Without a sync the two panels would solve different Riemann problems for
the same face and the fluxes would not cancel. snapy sends each panel's interior-side state to the neighbour, which
overwrites its ghost-side state with it; then both hold the same pair. Because a panel edge can join two edges of the
same orientation, where one panel's "left" is the other's "right" in the other panel's frame, the two states travel
under keys whose suffix selects the direction, and the receiving block assigns the role in its own frame. The scalar
once used a single key that swapped the states at those edges and made the solver pick the downwind state
([chengcli/snapy#220](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/issues/220)).

### Derivation

The argument is in `sources/canoe__tracer_seam_TECH_REPORT.md` §4 to §6; it is stated here against the code. In a
block's own frame, at its last face along $+x_2$ the left state $q^{\mathrm L}$ comes from its interior and the right
state $q^{\mathrm R}$ from its ghosts; at its first face the reverse. The pack and unpack rules for a key with a suffix
are:

- a key ending `:+` is sent only toward a direction with no negative offset and received only from a direction with
  no positive offset;
- a key ending `:-` is the mirror image.

The rules are the `suffix` tests in the cross-panel pack ([`cubed_sphere_layout.cpp:710-719`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp#L710-L719)) and the
`suffix` tests in the unpack ([`cubed_sphere_layout.cpp:924-932`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp#L924-L932)). With $q^{\mathrm L}$ sent as `hydro_wl:+` and $q^{\mathrm R}$ as
`hydro_wr:-`, a block sends from its last face only $q^{\mathrm L}$, its interior state there, and from its first face
only $q^{\mathrm R}$, again its interior state. A neighbour that lies on the receiver's negative side delivers into the
receiver's $q^{\mathrm L}$; one on its positive side into $q^{\mathrm R}$. Both rules are evaluated in the receiver's
own frame, so at an edge where both panels see the other on their positive side the interior state of the sender lands
in the receiver's $q^{\mathrm R}$, which in the receiver's frame is the side the sender occupies. In every case the
ghost-side state at a shared face is replaced by the neighbour's interior state, and the two blocks hold the same
ordered pair. Nothing is approximated.

### Numerical method

The sync runs inside each stage, after the $x_2$ and $x_3$ reconstruction and before the solves. Both directions are
begun, launched and finalised together. The options are `cross_panel_only(true)`, `interpolate(false)` and
`type(kPrimitive)`, with `dim` set to the direction, so only the one face layer at panel edges moves; the
velocity frame rotation of @sec-ch03-csinterp is applied to the states, the reverse flag reorders the strip along the
edge, and the flip and transpose flags are no-ops on a strip one face deep. The scalar runs the same sync with
`type(kScalar)` before its own solves. @fig-ch03-cslrsync-roles draws the roles at a same-orientation edge.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-cslrsync-roles
#| fig-cap: "Left and right states at a face shared by two panels whose edges have the same orientation. Each panel's interior-side state (filled triangle) is sent; each ghost-side state (open triangle) is overwritten with the neighbour's interior state, so both panels hold the same pair."
#| fig-alt: "Two cells on either side of a face, each panel's own axis arrow pointing toward the face, with triangles marking the exchanged states."
#| echo: false
```

: Code map of the face-state seam sync. {#tbl-ch03-cslrsync-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-cslrsync-code):

1. After `precon23` reconstructs the $x_2$ states, the hydro puts them in `send_vars2` under `hydro_wl:+` and
   `hydro_wr:-` and begins the exchange; the same for $x_3$ ([`hydro_forward.cpp:542-570`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L542-L570)).
2. It launches both and finalises both with `finalize_exchange` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:572-587`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L572-L587)); the solves
   follow.
3. The scalar does the same with `scalar_wl:+` and `scalar_wr:-` ([`scalar.cpp:80-125`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/scalar/scalar.cpp#L80-L125)).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_flux_covariance_seams_python` | six panels with the #289 term on conserve mass, vapour and $E+\mathrm{PE}$ over the run | $10^{-12}$ relative drift | `DRIFT_TOL` in the script |
| `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_python` | tracer mass is conserved across seams and the hat stays in $[0,1]$ | $10^{-13}$ drift | `DRIFT_TOL`, @sec-ch03-thetacopy |

: Tests that exercise the face-state sync. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-cslrsync-tests}

The conservation arm is `arm_conservation` and its threshold `DRIFT_TOL`
([`test_flux_covariance_seams.py:34-93`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_flux_covariance_seams.py#L34-L93)); a shared face whose two panels solved different problems would leak
and fail it. There is no dedicated test of the suffix rule itself. The tests run on CPU in one process. Their pass
status at the pin was not run for this chapter (missing evidence).

### Limits

No known limits. The transpose and flip flags are computed for these strips but have no effect on a strip one face
deep (read from the code). The suffix rule has no direct unit test (not measured). The switch combinations that are
tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix of chapter 12.
